calls.head: The Wild can’t afford to take penalties
calls.body: The Wild’s penalty kill is around the middle of the league, and the Bruins’ power play is near the top of the league. Discipline matters more than usual for the Wild tonight.
calls.call: The Bruins’ power play creates at least their usual 7.7 expected goals per 60.
calls.nums: Boston 9th for power play (7.7 expected goals per 60) · Minnesota 22nd for penalty kill
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 2 and 1 games this season
calls.happened: Boston’s power play created 8.5 expected goals per 60 in 5:59 of 5-on-4 time, against their usual 7.7, and scored 0 goals.

calls.head: The Bruins should pile up the shots
calls.body: The Bruins shoot a lot, and the Wild are around the middle of the league at keeping shots down. Look for a big shot total.
calls.call: The Bruins take at least their usual 59.1 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5.
calls.nums: Boston 10th for shot volume (59.1 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5) · Minnesota 22nd for shot suppression
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 2 and 1 games this season
calls.happened: Boston took 47.0 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5 (adjusted for score and venue), against their usual 59.1.

calls.head: Expect a track meet
calls.body: Boston plays some of the league’s fastest games, and so does Minnesota. We think this one runs hotter than either team’s usual.
calls.call: The game runs at more than 85.2 shots per 60 at 5-on-5, faster than either team’s usual.
calls.nums: Pace (shots per 60 at 5-on-5, both teams): Boston 7th (83.5), Minnesota 3rd (85.2)
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 2 and 1 games this season
calls.happened: The game ran at 71.3 shots per 60 at 5-on-5, both teams combined, against the faster team’s usual 85.2 and a league average of 81.9.

calls.head: The Wild get in close; the Bruins shoot from distance
calls.body: The Wild are near the top of the league for shots from in close, at the close-range end; the Bruins are one of the league’s worst, at the long-range end. Expect that gap to show.
calls.call: The Wild take a bigger share of their shots from within 20 feet than the Bruins.
calls.nums: Shots from in close: Minnesota 6th, Boston 29th
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 2 and 1 games this season
calls.happened: On share of 5-on-5 shots from within 20 feet, Minnesota had 32% and Boston 37%. Coming in, Minnesota was at 32% and Boston at 29%.

MIN.head: We gave Minnesota a 77% chance, and Minnesota delivered.

BOS.head: We gave Boston only a 23% chance, and it went the way we feared.

surprises.head: Minnesota leaned on their bottom six
surprises.body: Minnesota’s bottom-six forwards played 47% of the forwards’ 5-on-5 time, against their usual 42% and a league average of 42%. A team strays this far about once every 25 games.

story.head: The Wild beat the Bruins
paras: Tanner Jeannot opened the scoring 1:53 in. Kirill Kaprizov added two goals.
The chances were closer than the score.

items.text: One of the preview’s four calls held.
